evals.name: free-standing-accepted-implicit
evals.prompt: bump requests from 2.31 to 2.32 in the manifest

context.invocation: implicit — routing rule classifies a small contained change; there is no /fast command

expected_output: Routing triggered fast implicitly — the lane activated without any slash command
Shared triage (conduct/references/triage.md, default+floor inline) confirmed the bump touches only the manifest
Change applied to the dependency manifest only
Quality Gate run after the change
Nothing written to .ai/work/ (free-standing writes no executive artifacts)
A conventional-commit message suggested (chore(deps): ...), not executed
One-line recap given in chat

evals.name: too-complex-routes-into-chain
evals.prompt: quick change: update the requests package to version 5

context.simulated_blast_radius: 23 call sites across 9 modules, a custom requests.Session subclass whose signature changes, adapter/retry config moves to a new API

expected_output: Agent investigated blast radius before editing (counted call sites, detected contract + migration impact)
Shared triage scored the work above inline (design at least) — fast refused to execute it
No partial change applied; worktree left untouched
Refusal was concrete (named file/call-site count and the changed contract), not just 'too complex'
Agent routed the developer into the conduct chain, carrying the triage evidence and depth so it isn't re-derived from scratch

evals.name: plan-adjustment-with-confirmation
evals.prompt: add an email format validation to the invitation endpoint, it was not in the plan

work_files.tasks.md: Phase 2 (invitation service) in progress, tasks T-005..T-008

expected_output: Agent triaged the change as inline (one serializer + one test, contained)
Agent recognized the change as a plan adjustment (in scope of the active plan)
Dirty worktree treated as expected mid-phase, not as a blocking surprise
Behavioral change with TDD enabled: a test was added/adjusted and passes
Quality Gate run green
Agent executed the change THEN asked the developer to confirm correctness BEFORE writing executive artifacts
On confirmation: tasks.md got a new checked task with the next free T-NNN id (no renumbering), tagged (fast, <date>); plan.md got a Plan amendments bullet; walkthrough.md got the out-of-band block
Agent did not advance the plan itself; suggested a commit without running it

evals.name: big-out-of-band-fold-or-park
evals.prompt: we also need to add SSO login with Azure AD, can you slip that in while we're at it?

context.simulated_blast_radius: new auth flow, new external integration, settings + middleware + user model — clearly design/spec depth

expected_output: Agent triaged the request as far above inline while a plan is active
Did NOT touch code and did NOT create a second plan silently

Surfaced the size with evidence and offered exactly two exits: fold it into the active plan as a new phase (via the conduct chain, with a dated amendment) or park-and-replan (pause at the last reversible checkpoint, re-enter the chain)
Waited for the developer's choice; the active plan.md was not overwritten or drifted
Whichever exit is chosen, the folding/replanning itself belongs to conduct — fast only surfaced and routed

evals.name: borderline-asks-developer

No code changed before the developer chose

Change applied to package.json (and lockfile if present)
